title: Senior Schedule Balance Planner
creator: Beth Kullberg
subject: College Admissions
description: Build a draft senior schedule and weekly commitments, then compare the rigor signal it sends with the weekly hours it demands, to find a sustainable plan.

learningObjectives: Students will judge whether a draft senior schedule balances rigor against workload by comparing its rigor signal with its estimated weekly hours, and adjust it to reach a sustainable plan.
prerequisites: Chapter 7: Your Senior Year Course Load

controls: Six course-level dropdowns with core checkboxes
Job, activity, and application hour sliders

keyQuestions: Why can a 'very demanding' schedule be a stronger choice than the 'most demanding' one?
What happens to the rigor signal when you drop a core subject?
Where in your week do application hours come from?
commonMisconceptions: More APs are always better for admission.
Senior year workload is the same as junior year's.
assessmentOpportunities: Students propose a senior schedule that is at least demanding with a load under 50 hours and justify one trade-off they made.
